newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pick'n Pay picks Boland as partner.
newsitem.headline: Pick'n Pay picks Boland as partner.

text.p: South Africa's leading supermarket chain Pick 'n Pay said on Wednesday it had selected Boland Bank as its partner for its launch into the financial services market later this year.
Managing director Gareth Ackerman said the deal could be developed across a full range of financial services in the future.

"There will be a banking product, we hope towards the middle of the year. Then at a future stage, either with Boland or other players in market, we may launch unit trusts or insurance," Ackerman told Reuters.
"We don't see ourselves taking on the big banks -- we see it as complementary."
Pick 'n Pay said Boland had won the tender against competition from the country's "big four" banks, in part due to its ability to meet the technology demands the retailer required.
Ackerman stressed that the partnership with Boland Bank did not signify a closer relationship with Shoprite or Pep Stores.
Boland managing director Michiel le Roux welcomed the contract: "The deal is just what we needed to provide the platform for us to move into the new phase in banking."
Boland is shortly to merge with NBS Bank.
